agentic-coding.context.give-delegated-ag.title: Give Delegated Agents the Context They Need to Decide
agentic-coding.context.give-delegated-ag.applies_when: another agent is about to receive a bounded task that requires judgment about scope, tradeoffs, or quality, and important user corrections or accepted decisions are not visible in the files the agent will inspect

agentic-coding.context.write-decision-de.title: Write a Checkpoint That Preserves Decisions
agentic-coding.context.write-decision-de.applies_when: a long pause, context reduction, or session boundary is imminent, and the agent must create a durable checkpoint without carrying exploratory noise into the resumed task

agentic-coding.correction.restore-author.title: Reset the Work After a Confirmed Correction
agentic-coding.correction.restore-author.applies_when: an authorized user correction, accepted scope change, or rejection of unrequested behavior has made part of the current work obsolete, and the agent is about to continue from the old interpretation

agentic-coding.delivery.claim-only-suppo.title: Claim Only What the Evidence Proves
agentic-coding.delivery.claim-only-suppo.applies_when: the agent is about to say that work is complete, fixed, accepted, deployed, pushed, or verified, and the available evidence may cover only a narrower artifact state or technical slice

agentic-coding.delivery.report-material-.title: Report Only Remaining Issues That Matter
agentic-coding.delivery.report-material-.applies_when: delivery or handoff is imminent, at least one known limitation, risk, plan deviation, or unfinished item could change the recipient's next decision, and the agent must decide what to report

agentic-coding.implementation.choose-sma.title: Choose the Least Complex Design That Fully Works
agentic-coding.implementation.choose-sma.applies_when: two or more implementation designs can satisfy the required behavior, and the agent must choose how much new abstraction, state, indirection, or I/O the current change actually needs

agentic-coding.implementation.confirm-pr.title: Confirm What Users Can Depend On
agentic-coding.implementation.confirm-pr.applies_when: accepted scope authorizes a long-lived UI control, API, configuration value, stored value, public export, source type, or extension category, but the agent is about to expose an exact variant that the accepted scope does not define

agentic-coding.implementation.inspect-an.title: Check What Already Exists Before Building
agentic-coding.implementation.inspect-an.applies_when: implementation is about to add a helper or mechanism, and the agent has not yet determined whether a nearby module, declared dependency, or the runtime already provides the required behavior under the current constraints

agentic-coding.implementation.justify-ad.title: Justify Added Checks Before Implementing Them
agentic-coding.implementation.justify-ad.applies_when: the agent is considering new or stronger validation, preflight checks, permission confirmations, integrity scans, or blocking prerequisites while implementing a backend request, local HTTP client, startup, shutdown, or repair command, before deciding whether to add them

agentic-coding.implementation.limit-inve.title: Limit Investigation to the Current Decision
agentic-coding.implementation.limit-inve.applies_when: the target file, symbol, or behavior is known, but the agent is about to inspect additional code, tests, configuration, documentation, logs, or analogous modules without naming a current decision that their contents could change

agentic-coding.implementation.make-recov.title: Give Recovery One Owner and an Explicit Outcome
agentic-coding.implementation.make-recov.applies_when: a failed operation is about to gain retries, defaults, alternate sources, degraded results, or catch-and-continue wrappers, and the agent must decide whether that recovery preserves the caller's promised outcome

agentic-coding.implementation.preserve-r.title: Put Shared Rules in the Responsible Component
agentic-coding.implementation.preserve-r.applies_when: a change crosses a domain, layer, package, service, or repository boundary, and the agent must decide which component should own a rule that must remain consistent across more than one caller or entry point

agentic-coding.implementation.replan-on-.title: Replan When New Facts Change the Work
agentic-coding.implementation.replan-on-.applies_when: coding has revealed an unplanned dependency, public behavior, stored state, I/O path, risk, or verification need that changes the accepted scope, and the agent is about to continue under the old plan

agentic-coding.implementation.surface-un.title: Make Safe Temporary Assumptions Explicit
agentic-coding.implementation.surface-un.applies_when: one implementation detail remains uncertain, and the agent is about to use a temporary interpretation that is low-impact, reversible, and does not change a public contract, security boundary, or irreversible operation

agentic-coding.implementation.validate-a.title: Validate at the Boundary That Owns the Fact
agentic-coding.implementation.validate-a.applies_when: a fact is checked or normalized across adapters, internal HTTP handoffs, services, or storage, and the agent must assign its owning boundary and determine which established results remain valid at later locations

agentic-coding.planning.decide-scope-and.title: Decide Scope and Stop Conditions Before Work Begins
agentic-coding.planning.decide-scope-and.applies_when: committed work is about to begin and adjacent improvements could extend execution without a recorded finish, defer, or replan boundary, whether candidate items still lack admission reasons or the scope is already fixed

agentic-coding.planning.derive-committed.title: Derive the Committed Set from Concerns
agentic-coding.planning.derive-committed.applies_when: a decision-bearing set — plan items, acceptance criteria, checklists, definition-of-done lists, standards, checks, rules, or scoring dimensions that will determine what is built, what passes, what scores, or what is allowed — is being formed or revised by adding, merging, or removing items, whether working alone or in discussion

agentic-coding.planning.keep-acceptance-.title: Keep the Acceptance Path Completable
agentic-coding.planning.keep-acceptance-.applies_when: proposed validation, authorization, permission, confirmation, readiness, or compatibility checks must be composed into a required user workflow, including backend startup, shutdown, repair, or recovery, and the agent must walk whether the acceptance scenario can complete through their combined effects

agentic-coding.planning.map-plan-to-user.title: Map the Plan to User Capability
agentic-coding.planning.map-plan-to-user.applies_when: a plan that spans interfaces, services, storage, or other boundaries is about to be finalized, and nobody has traced its tasks end to end against the complete requested behavior path

agentic-coding.planning.plan-sufficient-.title: Plan the Minimum Sufficient Evidence
agentic-coding.planning.plan-sufficient-.applies_when: acceptance conditions are known and implementation is about to begin, but the agent has not chosen observations that can distinguish success from plausible failure at an appropriate cost

agentic-coding.planning.scale-work-to-ri.title: Scale Work to Risk and Cost
agentic-coding.planning.scale-work-to-ri.applies_when: an implementation approach has been selected, and the agent is about to set its investigation, validation, review, and recovery depth without weighing affected users, reversibility, uncertainty, and failure cost

agentic-coding.recovery.reground-after-c.title: Reground After Context Loss
agentic-coding.recovery.reground-after-c.applies_when: work is resuming after context reduction, interruption, or a same-agent session pause, and the agent is about to edit or report status using a summary that has not been checked against the current request, files, and results

agentic-coding.recovery.validate-handoff.title: Validate Handoffs Before Continuing
agentic-coding.recovery.validate-handoff.applies_when: another agent, contributor, or delegated task has returned conclusions or completion status, and the receiver is about to rely on them without checking the current request, files, commit, and cited results

agentic-coding.requirements.define-accep.title: Define Acceptance and Explicit Non-goals
agentic-coding.requirements.define-accep.applies_when: the requested result is clear and implementation is about to be planned, but no current list states which behaviors must work at completion and which tempting extensions sit outside it

agentic-coding.requirements.ground-user-.title: Ground Work in the User Goal
agentic-coding.requirements.ground-user-.applies_when: work is about to be framed or continued and no current sentence states the observable result the affected user or operator needs, while the easiest nearby component offers to define the task instead

agentic-coding.requirements.resolve-sour.title: Resolve Authority Across Conflicting Sources
agentic-coding.requirements.resolve-sour.applies_when: two or more governing sources for the same behavior disagree — request, spec or contract, decision record, plan, README, code, or tests — and one of them is about to be treated as the intended behavior

agentic-coding.review.run-subtractive-re.title: Remove Unneeded Changes Before Commit
agentic-coding.review.run-subtractive-re.applies_when: a completed implementation diff is about to be committed or handed off, and its added files, abstractions, fallbacks, interfaces, I/O, tests, or documents have not been checked for a current reason to remain

agentic-coding.review.validate-findings-.title: Validate Findings Before Taking Action
agentic-coding.review.validate-findings-.applies_when: a human, agent, analyzer, or review has raised a finding, and the agent is about to change the current artifact without first establishing whether the finding is true and in scope

agentic-coding.testing.anchor-tests-to-r.title: Anchor Each Test to a Contract
agentic-coding.testing.anchor-tests-to-r.applies_when: the agent is selecting tests for new or changed behavior and must decide what requirement, public contract, or domain invariant each proposed test is supposed to protect

agentic-coding.testing.assert-observable.title: Assert Observable or Stable Behavior
agentic-coding.testing.assert-observable.applies_when: a test already has a protected requirement or invariant, and the agent must choose an assertion boundary that distinguishes the promised outcome from incidental implementation details

agentic-coding.testing.classify-failure-.title: Classify Failures Before Changing Tests
agentic-coding.testing.classify-failure-.applies_when: a test, lint, type, build, or validation check has failed and the agent is about to change production code, the test, generated files, or configuration without first identifying the source of the disagreement

agentic-coding.testing.justify-regressio.title: Require Evidence for Regression Protection
agentic-coding.testing.justify-regressio.applies_when: a failure has been classified or a correction accepted, and the agent must decide whether to add a long-lived regression test, negative assertion, lint rule, or gate that will constrain future changes

agentic-coding.verification.bind-evidenc.title: Reuse Evidence Only When It Still Applies
agentic-coding.verification.bind-evidenc.applies_when: the agent is about to cite or reuse a verification result obtained before relevant code, configuration, dependencies, generated files, environment, or external conditions may have changed

agentic-coding.verification.close-or-dec.title: Resolve Missing Verification Results
agentic-coding.verification.close-or-dec.applies_when: comparison with the acceptance criteria shows that a required behavior has no adequate result, and the agent must decide whether to run another check, ask to reduce the promised scope, or report the work incomplete

agentic-coding.verification.map-evidence.title: Map Evidence to Acceptance Criteria
agentic-coding.verification.map-evidence.applies_when: implementation is ready for verification, actual checks or observations are available, and the agent is about to decide which acceptance criteria those results cover

practice.title: Justify Added Checks Before Implementing Them
practice.applies_when: the agent is considering new or stronger validation, preflight checks, permission confirmations, integrity scans, or blocking prerequisites while implementing a backend request, local HTTP client, startup, shutdown, or repair command, before deciding whether to add them
practice.body:
## When to apply

**Use before deciding to add or strengthen a check, not only when reviewing it after implementation.**
Trigger when drafting a plan or when an ordinary task leads the agent to propose a precaution of its
own. The task need not mention gates, duplication, or cost. A first check can be unjustified even
when it duplicates nothing and does not make the happy path impossible.

## Guidance

1. Name the failure the proposed check would prevent: the actual input, caller, state change, or
   fault that can reach this operation, and who would be harmed. Identify any mandatory contract or
   policy separately; a generic risk category is not a failure path.
2. Find the guarantee's owner and existing coverage. Determine what ingress validation, producer
   postconditions, authorization, transactions, installation, or publication already establishes,
   and what can invalidate that fact before use. Localhost, a type cast, or an earlier check alone
   proves no continuing guarantee.
3. State the added protection: which still-reachable failure would escape without this check?
   Distinguish a new trust, conversion, or concurrent-state boundary from another copy of the same
   rule. Investigate an unknown security or data-loss exposure before treating it as absent.
4. Compare that protection with the check's own effects: false refusal, latency and I/O, maintenance,
   unavailable service, and blocked startup, upgrade, shutdown, or repair. Use a bounded observation
   when actual cost could change the choice; no benchmark or risk-report ritual is required.
5. Add or retain necessary protection; otherwise narrow its scope, choose a sufficient nonblocking
   response, move it only if the required guarantee survives, or omit it. Record the reason briefly
   in the existing design or review. Fewer checks is not the goal.

Stop with a justified choice about this proposed check before implementing it. If necessity is
settled and only its location is open, use boundary ownership instead. If several justified checks
must be composed into a usable workflow, walk the acceptance path rather than repeating this decision.

## Anti-pattern

A routine backend task leads the agent to add a full model-directory hash scan before every launch,
a second business-schema walk after every controlled HTTP response, and a healthy-service probe
before repair. Each is described as safer. Nobody names protection beyond the selected model's
loader, the response producer's established contract, or repair's own identity and permission checks.
Unused files now delay startup, valid results gain another rejection policy, and repair cannot run
when the service is broken. Reviewing each check only after implementation misses the earlier choice.

## Why

A plausible precaution can add work and new refusal paths without closing a real gap. Making its
necessity a separate decision catches that proposal before the agent commits to it; placing checks
correctly or proving a happy path later does not answer whether to add them in the first place.

## Exceptions and boundaries

Required security, data consistency, and contracts constrain the choice; expense does not authorize
removing them. Retain external-input checks, resource-specific authorization, atomic concurrent-state
protection, required native/model quality and release integrity, and recovery identity. Independently
justified defense in depth remains valid. Change an accepted checking contract through its owner,
not by silently downgrading a failure to a warning.

This is not a production bypass, a new user-approval requirement, or a general ban on startup scans.
A mutable imported model may need verification that an immutable installation does not. A repair
operation may work without business readiness but must still establish its own authorization,
identity, and mutation safety. Types and contract tests do not substitute for real trust boundaries.

## Example

A task connects a desktop client to its bundled local worker. The worker constructs validated records,
the session is authenticated, and responses are serialized without later mutation. Before adding a
second full business-schema traversal, the agent finds no new failure it would catch and omits it,
while retaining decoding, protocol matching, identity, and request correlation. The public import
route still validates arbitrary JSON; it does not inherit the bundled worker's guarantee.

A read-only desktop launch is about to gain its first free-disk-space threshold for a possible
future export feature. It duplicates no check and introduces no dependency cycle. The agent declines
it before coding: launch performs no substantial write, and no accepted contract requires the
threshold, so a supported read-only session would gain a new refusal without added protection.
Required startup input, native/model, and release-integrity checks remain; a mutable model still
needs protection against changes between verification and use.

anti_patterns.name: A precaution without added protection
anti_patterns.description: Adding a precaution before naming a reachable failure or mandatory contract and comparing its extra protection with false rejection, runtime work, availability, and recovery cost.

decisions.decision: Do not introduce the proposed free-space threshold before opening the desktop window. Preserve the supported read-only session; optional logging may be disabled if it cannot write.
decisions.reachable_failure_and_coverage: Under the supplied facts, launch reads existing content and has no download, export or substantial write to protect with this threshold. A possible future export is not a current launch requirement; the threshold establishes no needed launch guarantee.
decisions.tradeoff: The first check would introduce an unsupported refusal of an otherwise supported session. Lack of duplication does not justify that refusal. No measured performance claim is needed for this choice.
decisions.scope: This declines only the proposed disk threshold. It does not downgrade existing mandatory checks to warnings or decide requirements for a future export feature.

decisions.decision: Use the pinned bundled worker's validated-record guarantee for business schema; omit both the second full business-schema traversal and the executable hash on every status poll when their sole justification is the HTTP transport.
decisions.reachable_failure_and_coverage: The scenario guarantees authenticated worker sessions, producer validation and serialization without intervening mutation. Those facts, not localhost alone, establish the private producer guarantee. HTTP still requires client decoding, protocol checks and request correlation, but the proposed full traversal names no additional reachable schema failure under these assumptions. Hashing the executable per poll is not justified merely by transport choice.
decisions.tradeoff: The additions repeat schema work or file I/O and create extra failure paths without an identified added guarantee. This is qualitative design reasoning, not measured cost evidence.
retained_required_protections: Authenticated session and bundled worker identity/pinning
Producer business-schema validation and no-mutation serialization guarantee
Client decoding and rejection of undecodable responses
Any required installation or release integrity at its owning boundary
Independent validation of arbitrary JSON on the public import route
decisions.scope: No general trust in HTTP, localhost or type assertions is inferred; the unchecked schema path is limited to the guaranteed producer. No blanket integrity bypass is introduced.

decisions.decision: Exclude repair from the proposed universal inference-readiness prerequisite. Before repair mutates anything, use the existing local controller to establish installation/process identity, caller permission, the intended target path and exclusive mutation ownership independently of the business endpoint.
decisions.reachable_failure_and_coverage: A missing model can make inference unavailable, which is precisely the state repair must handle. A readiness response supplies no substitute for repair identity, permission or mutation safety and would block the legitimate recovery path. The stated controller already supplies those required prerequisites without readiness.
decisions.tradeoff: Reject the circular availability dependency, not the safety boundaries. Repair remains blocked when its own identity, authorization, target or exclusivity cannot be established.
retained_required_protections: Exclusive mutation ownership through the repair mutation
decisions.acceptance_path: Unhealthy inference -> independent controller safety checks -> authorized exclusive repair -> trusted-source, model-acceptance and publication-integrity success -> allow inference to resume. Any failed mandatory protection prevents resumption; unavailable inference alone does not prevent repair.

decisions.decision: Add strict validation at public JSON ingress and resource-specific tenant authorization, require atomic protection for publication of the same version, and require artifact integrity plus signature verification on the actual downloaded bytes before publication. Do not inherit the private worker's schema shortcut.
decisions.reachable_failure_and_coverage: Public JSON has no trusted producer schema guarantee; token validity alone does not authorize the named tenant resource. Independent preflights leave a race between two publishers. Truncated or substituted bytes violate the explicit artifact integrity and signature contract. Each proposed protection therefore closes a stated trust or concurrent-state gap rather than repeating an established guarantee.
concrete_boundary_design: Parse and validate the public JSON's required structure and business constraints before accepting it; reject invalid input.
Authenticate the caller and authorize the particular named resource against that caller's tenant; a valid token is necessary but insufficient.

Stage the candidate without making it a published release, and verify artifact integrity and the required trusted signature on the exact candidate bytes to be published. Keep that candidate from changing between verification and publication.

Use a single atomic conditional publication operation or a version-keyed exclusive publication critical section with an atomic commit. The final version-existence/conflict check and publication belong in that protected operation, not only in preflight; at most one conflicting publisher can commit. A losing request must not overwrite or expose a partial release.
decisions.tradeoff: Validation, authorization, synchronization and cryptographic work have costs, but the stated trust boundaries, concurrency hazard and mandatory contract justify them. Costs cannot authorize removal or warning-only treatment of these protections.
retained_required_protections: Protection against changes between verification and use
Existing security, consistency and release contracts remain mandatory

evidence_limits: All case facts are scenario assumptions, not observations of product behavior or security guarantees.
The only executed program commands were the recorded public CLI query and get. No hypothetical implementation or product behavior was executed.

One keyword query returned three practice IDs; one full relevant body was fetched once, read before all decisions, and reused for the later three cases. The other two bodies were not retrieved, and no per-case queries were manufactured.
The returned sourcePath is CLI result metadata only; no raw Pack content, repository README/SOURCES, fixture rubric, other arm or other agent artifact was read.

This single fresh catalog-only session shows a chosen lookup and subsequent design reasoning. It does not establish stable automatic routing, comparative effectiveness or causal improvement from correct decisions.
No actual host Plugin deployment occurred.

No pack, source, fixture, user configuration or Store was edited; no build, lint, tests, formatters or product smoke commands were run. The requested JSON artifact is the only project file created by this assignment.
No grading against unseen expectations was performed.

practice.title: Validate at the Boundary That Owns the Fact
practice.applies_when: a fact is checked or normalized across adapters, internal HTTP handoffs, services, or storage, and the agent must assign its owning boundary and determine which established results remain valid at later locations
practice.body:
## When to apply

Apply when assigning a needed check to its owner or deciding whether a fact must be re-established
at a later handoff. Trace the actual path, not every package. Whether a proposed precaution supplies
enough added protection to justify its costs is the separate `justify-added-checks` decision.
Choosing a retry or fallback after a known failure is a recovery decision.

## Guidance

1. Trace the relevant input or state and its handoffs only. Name the reachable failure or mandatory
   contract each check addresses, the fact it establishes, where that fact first becomes trustworthy,
   and the component responsible for keeping it true.
2. Assign each check to its owning boundary: validate external shape at ingress, apply business
   rules where their state is owned, normalize into the agreed representation once at its owning
   conversion, and pass the established result through ordinary internal calls. An internal type
   should express that result where practical; a cast alone establishes nothing.
3. Before adding another check, identify what could invalidate the earlier result at this location:
   another entry point, untrusted deserialization, a transformation, concurrent mutation, expired
   authorization, or an independently required protection. Keep the check only when such a condition
   exists — a new function, layer, or package name is not itself a new boundary.
4. Pass established facts through unchanged calls and keep checks at genuinely distinct boundaries.
   Remove duplicate internal work rather than adding caches, trusted flags, or locks to preserve it.

Stop with a clear owner per fact and only the checks the actual path needs; a short explanation in
the existing design or review is enough.

For a controlled internal producer, trust the postconditions its contract and real production path
establish. A process hop or local HTTP call alone does not make the payload independently
untrusted. Keep decoding, authentication, protocol matching, and request–response correlation where
needed; they do not imply repeating the complete business schema. A representation conversion
justifies checks for failures it introduces, not every failure imaginable for an arbitrary object.

Do not make protection against another internal implementation violating its types and contract a
default production responsibility. Prefer types, producer contract tests, and necessary development
assertions. A mock that invents an output the producer cannot emit does not justify a downstream
guard. Preserve tests for reachable external input, real corruption, and supported recovery.

Once JSON has been decoded and validated without introducing new values, checking for cycles,
Symbols, or arbitrary object prototypes establishes no new fact. Retain adapters that own a real
conversion or lifecycle; distinct boundaries need not share one validator. Earlier verification
does not cover later file changes or a new caller that can bypass the verified path.

Preserve external input validation, model/native integration quality checks, publication integrity,
transaction and snapshot consistency, authentication, process ownership, and regeneration of
corrupt derived caches. Change an accepted checking contract through its normal change process
before removing its required checks.

## Anti-pattern

An HTTP adapter parses a quantity into a positive integer. A service, domain helper, and repository
each accept that typed value, but independently parse, clamp, and reject it because each module is
meant to be robust. Their limits later drift: the adapter accepts a bulk order while a hidden helper
silently clamps it. Every layer has tests, yet a valid request is changed after acceptance and the
caller cannot tell which rule defines the order.

## Why

A check adds value when it establishes a fact that can actually be false there. Repeating an already
established fact creates more rule owners, failure paths, and maintenance without improving the
guarantee. Distinct boundaries can still need distinct protections even when they inspect the same
field.

## Exceptions and boundaries

An API and CLI may each validate raw input before sharing a typed domain call. A database uniqueness
constraint remains necessary when a preflight check cannot prevent concurrent inserts. A worker
deserializing a queued message has a new input boundary; an unchanged object passed to a private
helper does not. Encoding for HTML output solves a different problem from parsing input.

Use confirmed deployment and caller facts when sizing authorization. An internal service behind an
enforced gateway need not recreate an identity platform for every helper; a bypassable gateway or
cross-tenant operation can require its own authorization decision. Retain separately justified
defense in depth and explicit policy requirements. Before removing existing checks, establish their
callers and contract; this Practice does not authorize changing accepted behavior by itself.

## Example

An inventory service accepts orders through an HTTP endpoint and a CSV import. Each adapter parses
its raw quantity and creates the same typed command. The domain service checks current available
stock, and the database atomically prevents competing reservations from overselling. The agent keeps
those distinct checks and removes a proposed third string parser in the repository: no string or
unchecked caller can reach it. A stock change still gets checked at the mutation boundary, while the
parsed quantity is passed through without another normalization policy.

anti_patterns.name: A defensive check in every layer
anti_patterns.description: Rechecking or normalizing the same established fact in every layer without a new input, mutation, caller, or failure mode, creating divergent rules and rejecting valid work.

practice.title: Keep the Acceptance Path Completable
practice.applies_when: proposed validation, authorization, permission, confirmation, readiness, or compatibility checks must be composed into a required user workflow, including backend startup, shutdown, repair, or recovery, and the agent must walk whether the acceptance scenario can complete through their combined effects
practice.body:
## When to apply

Apply while planning or implementing a workflow whose proposed checks must work together. Walk
normal operations, startup, shutdown, and supported repair or recovery commands, even when the task
never mentions gates. Completeness and added friction cover the required paths, including error,
repeat, and reopen cases. A single proposed check's necessity is the `justify-added-checks` decision;
this Practice decides how checks compose without making the accepted workflow unusable.

## Guidance

Write each acceptance condition as ordered steps from initiating action to observable result,
including every check the change adds. Walk all conditions for completeness: a required step with no
owner is a mapping gap and is resolved before weight. Walk the required paths for friction: every
added check that can reject, delay, or demand intervention is a gate. Give each gate the lowest rung
that still catches a failure you can name — observe (log), mark (annotate the result), confirm (ask
once, answerable where it fires), block (reject). A rung above observe is forced only by an actor
and path that exist in this deployment's facts or contracts; a risk category or generic attacker
forces nothing. Prefer narrowing a justified gate to the risky subset over gating the whole path.
Run the deletion test: name what concretely breaks, for whom, if the gate is removed; no answer
means remove the gate. A confirm nobody in this context can answer is a block — lower it or scope it
with a documented bypass. Then walk one failure: pick the check most likely to fail, let it fail
alone, and state what survives; if a single failure voids every other satisfied condition, name who
needs that severity and why attributed or partial results would mislead. Record the rung and the
named failure beside each gate's plan item. Stop when every acceptance condition completes with no
intervention beyond those acceptance or governing policy already name, and every gate names the
failure its rung blocks. For a change too small to plan, ask: can this added check block or delay a
required path, and what failure or mandatory policy justifies that effect? Keep justified blocks;
otherwise lower the rung, narrow the scope, or omit the check.

A repair command must not require the damaged index to be healthy; stopping an identified old
process need not require its business API to match the new client. Keep operation-specific
authorization, process identity, activity
protection, and consistency requirements. If a required safeguard conflicts with the recovery
contract, surface that conflict rather than bypassing it to make the command pass.

## Anti-pattern

A task adds a config-set command to a local CLI. The agent ships it with an allowlist of keys, a
path-traversal validator, an ownership permission check, and a confirmation prompt on every write.
The acceptance scenario — developer runs the command, config updates — now requires an interaction
and a grant the request never named, and scripts calling the CLI cannot answer the confirmation. The
calibration arrives after delivery, as deletion.

## Why

Per-item review sees each protection's story, never the composed path, and training prices visible
incidents above invisible unusability, so unwalked plans rationally over-protect. A Practice
improves only the dimension it names: completeness, friction, and failure composition must each be
walked to improve.

## Exceptions and boundaries

Governing policy or compliance can force a rung without local reachability — cite the policy, and
the gate stays. A real, reachable threat justifies block; this Practice calibrates and does not
remove justified protection. Pre-existing system guards are constraints, not deletion-test
candidates; if they make acceptance impossible, surface the conflict instead of removing them. Where
a check belongs and whether it duplicates another rule is a boundary-ownership question.

## Example

The config-set walkthrough writes the primary path with all four checks on: command, allowlist,
permission, confirmation, write, verify. Deletion tests: traversal input cannot reach a path, the OS
already enforces file ownership, and the confirmation catches typos acceptance does not name — all
drop or downgrade. One concern survives with evidence: overwriting the security-token key forces
re-authentication elsewhere. The gate narrows to a single confirm on that key subset; every other
key writes without interruption, and the change is logged.

A backend's repair command must rebuild a damaged derived index while the service is not ready.
The proposed shared readiness preflight rejects that exact state before repair begins. The agent
keeps readiness enforcement for ordinary queries but gives repair its own authorized path with the
required exclusive mutation protection. Repair can now rebuild the index without first querying it;
an unauthorized caller or a conflicting writer is still refused. No global "skip checks" switch is

details.decision: Give maintenance repair an operation-specific authorized controller path; do not require successful inference readiness as its preflight.

proposal_comparison.reachable_failure_or_contract: Missing model makes inference unavailable by the scenario's definition. Requiring that endpoint to be healthy blocks exactly the supported repair state and establishes none of repair's necessary authorization or mutation guarantees.
proposal_comparison.added_protection: No repair-specific protection from the shared inference readiness prerequisite; existing controller can establish the necessary independent facts.
proposal_comparison.cost_and_refusal: Creates a circular prerequisite and makes the accepted repair impossible.

owners.repair_authority: Existing local controller owns installation/process identity, caller permission, target path, and exclusive mutation ownership without the business endpoint.
owners.resumption_acceptance: Trusted-source verification, model acceptance, and publication integrity own the transition back to inference.

required_protections: Verify caller permission and intended target path.
Require trusted-source verification, model acceptance, and publication integrity before inference resumes.
Keep readiness requirements for ordinary inference; no global skip-checks bypass.
acceptance_path: Invoke maintenance repair while inference is unavailable.
Use the local controller to establish identity, caller permission, target path, and exclusive mutation ownership.
Repair the missing model without querying a healthy inference endpoint as a prerequisite.
Require trusted-source verification, model acceptance, and publication integrity before enabling inference again.
details.failure_walk: If permission, identity, target safety, or exclusivity fails, refuse mutation. If trusted-source/model/integrity acceptance fails, inference stays unavailable; repair's safe independent control path remains available. No required safeguard is downgraded to make recovery pass.

details.decision: Add external JSON validation, resource-specific tenant authorization, atomic concurrent publication protection, and required artifact integrity/signature verification at their actual owning boundaries; do not copy the private worker fast path.

proposal_comparison.reachable_failure_or_contract: Arbitrary JSON lacks a producer schema guarantee; a valid token can target another tenant; concurrent requests can both pass preflight and publish one version; downloaded bytes can be truncated or substituted, and integrity plus signature verification are mandatory.
proposal_comparison.added_protection: Each addition closes a distinct real gap or enforces an explicit contract: malformed/unaccepted input, cross-tenant access, publication races, and corrupted/substituted artifacts.
proposal_comparison.cost_and_refusal: Validation, authorization, synchronization, and cryptographic verification add work and can block unsafe requests. Those blocks are justified by the stated reachable failures and mandatory contract; overhead is not grounds to remove them.

owners.public_json: Public import ingress decodes and fully validates external shape/schema before using accepted values; private producer postconditions do not apply.
owners.resource_authorization: Resource-owning operation authorizes the caller against the requested tenant/resource, not merely token validity.
owners.publication_concurrency: Shared publication/mutation boundary atomically enforces one safe publication for the version, using a transaction/conditional publication or equivalent exclusive ownership covering the state change; a preflight alone is insufficient.
owners.artifact_verification: Verify required integrity and signature on the actual complete bytes to be published; keep those bytes unchanged through atomic publication, rather than verifying one object and later publishing replaceable bytes.

required_protections: Full validation of arbitrary public JSON.
Atomic consistency across concurrent same-version publication attempts.
Artifact integrity and signature verification before publication.
Preserve the guarantee between verified bytes and published bytes; retain existing contracts without downgrade.
acceptance_path: Decode and validate external JSON at ingress.
Authenticate and authorize the requested tenant/resource at its owning operation.
Download/stage bytes without publishing them; verify required integrity and signature on the bytes that will be committed.
At the mutation owner, atomically publish the verified version with concurrent-state protection that cannot be bypassed by two successful preflights.
Only a successful verified and atomic publication becomes visible; a conflicting attempt cannot overwrite or expose a partial/unverified version.
details.failure_walk: Malformed JSON or cross-tenant access is blocked before protected work. Truncation, substitution, or failed signature/integrity prevents publication. In a same-version race, the atomic boundary admits only a contract-valid outcome; the losing attempt does not expose partial data or overwrite the winner. These are justified blocking gates, not warnings.
details.implementation: Design only; no product code executed or changed.
